(464); Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (1221); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (310); Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. (11682); Sunan Ibn Majah, nos. (834, 835).]].

In the Name of Allah, the Entirely Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

The commentators differed here in many opinions. It was said: by "the fig" is meant the Mosque of Damascus. It was said: it is the fig itself. It was said: it is the mountain beside it.

Al-Qurtubi said: it is the Mosque of the People of the Cave [[Tafsir al-Qurtubi (20/111), from Muhammad ibn Ka'b.]].

Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that it is the Mosque of Noah which is on al-Judi.

Mujahid said: it is this fig of yours.

"And the olive": Ka'b al-Ahbar, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and others said: it is the Mosque of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

Mujahid and 'Ikrimah said: it is this olive from which you press oil.

"And Mount Sinin": Ka'b al-Ahbar and others said: it is the mountain on which Allah spoke to Musa.

"And this secure city": it means Makkah. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Hasan, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Ibn Zayd and Ka'b al-Ahbar. There is no disagreement regarding this.

Some of the imams said: these are three places, in each of which Allah sent a prophet from among the Ulu al-'Azm (the Steadfast Messengers), the possessors of the great legislations. The first: the place of the fig and the olive, which is Bayt al-Maqdis, in which Allah sent 'Isa ibn Maryam. The second: Tur Sinin, which is Tur Sinai, on which Allah spoke to Musa ibn 'Imran. The third: Makkah, which is the secure city, whoever enters it is safe, and in it Allah sent Muhammad (ﷺ).

They said: at the end of the Torah there is mention of these three places: "The Lord came from Sinai" — meaning the one on which Allah spoke to Musa [ibn 'Imran] [[Addition from M.]] — "and rose up from Sa'ir" — meaning Bayt al-Maqdis, from which Allah sent 'Isa — "and shone forth from the mountains of Paran" — meaning the mountains of Makkah, from which Allah sent Muhammad. [[In M: "reporting about them."]] He mentioned them in the existential order according to their sequence in time, and for this reason He swore by the most noble, then the more noble of it, then by the most noble of these two.

* *

His saying: "Indeed, We created man in the best of stature" is the thing sworn to, namely that He, exalted is He, created man in the best form and shape, upright in stature, with well-proportioned and beautiful limbs.

"Then We returned him to the lowest of the low" — that is, to the Fire. This was said by Mujahid, Abu al-'Aliyah, al-Hasan, Ibn Zayd and others. Then, after this beauty and freshness, his destination is the Fire if he does not obey Allah and follow the Messengers; for this reason He said: "Except those who believe and do righteous deeds."

Some of them said: "Then We returned him to the lowest of the low" means to the most abject age (senility). This was narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and 'Ikrimah — to the extent that 'Ikrimah said: whoever memorises the Qur'an will not be returned to the most abject age. Ibn Jarir chose this view. But if this were the meaning, the exception of the believers from it would not be fitting, since decrepitude may afflict some of them. The meaning is rather what we have mentioned, like His saying: "By time, indeed mankind is in loss, except those who believe and do righteous deeds" [Al-'Asr: 1-3].

* *

His saying: "So for them is a reward never to be cut off" — that is, uninterrupted, as has preceded.

Then He said: "So what causes you to deny the Recompense after this?" — meaning: O son of Adam, after this, what causes you to deny the Judgement (the Recompense) — that is, the reward in the Hereafter, when you have known the origination (of creation), and have recognised that whoever is able to originate creation is able to restore it all the more? So what compels you to deny the Return, when you know this?

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Sinan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Sufyan, from Mansur, who said: I said to Mujahid: "So what causes you to deny the Recompense after this?" Does it refer to the Prophet (ﷺ)? He said: God forbid! It refers to mankind. 'Ikrimah and others said likewise.

* *

His saying: "Is not Allah the most just of judges?" — that is, is He not the most judicious of judges, who does not oppress and does not wrong anyone? And from His justice is that He establishes the Resurrection, so that the wronged is given justice in this world against the one who wronged him. We have already mentioned in the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, traced to the Prophet: "When one of you recites: By the fig and the olive, and reaches its end: Is not Allah the most just of judges? then let him say: Yes, and I am of those who bear witness to that" [[See: the commentary on the last verse of Surah al-Qiyamah.]].

End of the Tafsir of [Surah] [[Addition from M, A.]] "Al-Tin and Al-Zaytun." And to Allah belongs all praise.
